title: Fish With Tomato, Olives, and Couscous
description: By Lidey Heuck: Flaky white fish and pearl couscous simmer together in a rich, smoky tomato sauce for a punchy one-pot dinner that comes together in just half an hour. The sauce relies heavily on pantry ingredients (think anchovies, roasted red peppers, crushed tomatoes and paprika); if you like more green on your dinner plate, a lemony arugula salad is a nice complement to the smoky flavors in this dish.
ingredients: ¼ cup olive oil, plus more for serving
¾ cup jarred roasted red peppers, roughly chopped, or 1 fresh red bell pepper, cored, seeded and diced
4 (6-ounce) skinless mild, white fish fillets, such as cod, fluke or halibut
½ cup olives, preferably black or Kalamata, pitted or not
2 tablespoons chopped fresh parsley, plus more for serving
2 teaspoons sherry vinegar or red wine vinegar
directions: In a large (12-inch) skillet (use one with a tight-fitting lid), heat the olive oil over medium. If using fresh red bell pepper, add it with the onion, and cook, tossing occasionally, until tender and lightly browned, 8 to 10 minutes. Meanwhile, pat the fish fillets dry with a paper towel and season with salt and pepper.

If using roasted red peppers, add them with the garlic, anchovies, paprika and cayenne, and cook for 1 more minute, until the garlic is fragrant. Add the wine and stir to scrape up any brown bits from the pan. When the wine has almost entirely evaporated, add the chicken stock, tomatoes, olives, parsley, 1 teaspoon salt and ½ teaspoon black pepper. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat.

Add the couscous, stir, turn the heat to low, cover and simmer for about 6 minutes. Then add the fish fillets, wiggling them lightly to submerge them in the sauce. Cover and cook until it’s tender and the liquid in the pan has reduced slightly, about 5 minutes or so more when the couscous is cooked and the fish is opaque and flakes easily with a fork. If you need any more liquid, add some water or wine or broth.

Plate the fish, being careful to keep it intact. Then, off the heat, stir in the little bit of vinegar into the couscous mixture before adding the sauce to the fish plate. Serve garnished with additional parsley and a drizzle of olive oil.
